title: Trump says he's working on 'a deal that's fair' with Canada

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump, flanked by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, right, and Vice President JD Vance, speaks during a press conference Friday at the White House. (Kylie Cooper/Reuters)

blocks.text: In a news conference at the White House on Friday after returning from his trip to Asia that included a brief meeting with Prime Minister Mark Carney, U.S. President Donald Trump floated the prospect of reaching a trade deal with Canada soon — but said more work needs to be done to get there.
'While more work remains to be done with Canada, Prime Minister Carney was very nice,' Trump tells reporters
U.S. President Donald Trump floated the prospect of reaching a trade deal with Canada soon but said more work needs to be done to get there.

In a news conference at the White House on Friday after returning from his trip to Asia that included a brief meeting with Prime Minister Mark Carney, Trump said he's working on a trade deal with Canada.

"While more work remains to be done with Canada, Prime Minister Carney was very nice," Trump told reporters. "One of the things he wants to do is build a Keystone pipeline for us — and we like that. But, you know, got to do a lot more than that."

Trump repeated several of his most frequently stated grievances, claiming Canada has been ripping off the U.S. for years and insisting his country doesn't need energy, vehicles or lumber from its northern neighbour.
"That being said, we're working on making a deal that's fair," Trump continued.

The U.S. president complained about the trade deficit with Canada, and put the figure at "about $80 billion." That's closer to the actual goods trade deficit (in 2025) of $48 billion US than the $200-billion figure he has often used.
"I said, when it's down to zero, come over and let's start talking," Trump said.
Canada pursues tariff relief through interim U.S. trade deal
Trump's comments come as the Carney government seeks an interim agreement with the U.S. aimed at bringing down some of the most onerous tariffs on Canadian exports.
Trump held his news conference with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vice-President JD Vance at his side.
In his own remarks, Rubio spoke of "unfairness and imbalance" in commercial relations with Canada.

"The president had an opportunity to visit with the prime minister and move the ball forward on getting to a final agreement that is good for American workers and fair to the United States of America," Rubio said.

Mike Crawley is a correspondent for CBC News, based in Washington. He began his career as a newspaper reporter in B.C., spent six years as a freelance journalist in various parts of Africa, then joined the CBC in 2005. Mike reported on Ontario politics for 15 years. He was born and raised in Saint John, N.B.
